question_text:
Consider a diffusion couple between pure tungsten and a tungsten alloy containing 1 at $\%$ thorium. After several minutes of exposure at $2000^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, a transition zone of 0.01 cm thickness is established. What is the flux of thorium atoms at this time if diffusion is due to (a) volume diffusion, (b) grain boundary diffusion, and (c) surface diffusion? Refer to Table for the diffusion coefficients and activation energies for thorium in tungsten. The lattice parameter of BCC tungsten is $3.165 \AA$. Give your answer as a tuple (volume diffusion flux, grain boundary diffusion flux, surface diffusion flux).

Table:
\begin{tabular}{|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline \multicolumn{5}{|l|}{TABLE 5-2 $\quad$ The effect of the type of diffusion for thorium in tungsten and for self-diffusion in silver} \\
\hline \multirow[b]{2}{*}{Diffusion Type} & \multicolumn{4}{|c|}{Diffusion Coefficient ( $D$ )} \\
\hline & \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{Thorium in Tungsten} & \multicolumn{2}{|c|}{Silver in Silver} \\
\hline & $D_0\left(\mathrm{~cm}^2 / \mathrm{s}\right)$ & $Q$ ( $\mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol}$ ) & $D_0\left(\mathrm{~cm}^2 / \mathrm{s}\right)$ & $Q(\mathrm{cal} / \mathrm{mol})$ \\
\hline Surface & 0.47 & 66,400 & 0.068 & 8,900 \\
\hline Grain boundary & 0.74 & 90,000 & 0.24 & 22,750 \\
\hline Volume & 1.00 & 120,000 & 0.99 & 45,700 \\
\hline \multicolumn{5}{|l|}{*Given by parameters for Equation 5-4.} \\
\hline
\end{tabular}The units of each required answer are (atoms/cm²·s, atoms/cm²·s, atoms/cm²·s), respectively.
response:
## Solution

**Setup:** For BCC tungsten (2 atoms/unit cell), the total atomic density is:

$$\frac{2}{a^3} = \frac{2}{(3.165\times10^{-8}\,\text{cm})^3} = 6.31\times10^{22}\;\text{atoms/cm}^3$$

**Concentration gradient:** The alloy side has 1 at% Th → $C_{\text{Th}} = 0.01 \times 6.31\times10^{22} = 6.31\times10^{20}$ atoms/cm³; the pure W side has 0. Across the 0.01 cm transition zone:

$$\frac{dC}{dx} = \frac{\Delta C}{\Delta x} = \frac{6.31\times10^{20}}{0.01} = 6.31\times10^{22}\;\text{atoms/cm}^4$$

**Diffusivities** at $T = 2273$ K via $D = D_0\exp(-Q/RT)$, with $RT = 1.987\times2273 = 4516$ cal/mol:

| Mechanism | $D_0$ | $Q$ | $D$ (cm²/s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Volume | 1.00 | 120,000 | $2.89\times10^{-12}$ |
| Grain boundary | 0.74 | 90,000 | $1.64\times10^{-9}$ |
| Surface | 0.47 | 66,400 | $1.94\times10^{-7}$ |

**Flux** via Fick's first law, $J = D\,(dC/dx)$:

- **(a) Volume:** $J = 2.89\times10^{-12}\times6.31\times10^{22} = 1.82\times10^{11}$ atoms/cm²·s
- **(b) Grain boundary:** $J = 1.64\times10^{-9}\times6.31\times10^{22} = 1.03\times10^{14}$ atoms/cm²·s
- **(c) Surface:** $J = 1.94\times10^{-7}\times6.31\times10^{22} = 1.22\times10^{16}$ atoms/cm²·s

The flux increases by ~2 orders of magnitude per mechanism as the activation barrier drops, reflecting the progressively easier short-circuit diffusion paths.

$$\boxed{\left(1.82\times10^{11},\;1.03\times10^{14},\;1.22\times10^{16}\right)}$$
